name: Labor Notes
what: Independent media and training project that teaches rank-and-file workers how to organize at work, run union campaigns and reform their unions.
legal_status: Nonprofit (Labor Education and Research Project); exact 501(c) type and EIN not read
partisanship: Independent of parties; pro-worker, rank-and-file movement (own description not quoted)
cost: Free articles and resources; paid conference registration; membership/donations optional
status_2026: Labor Notes 2026 Conference held June 12-14 (registration closed notice on official site); post-event article dated July 2026; The Nation coverage June 17, 2026.
notes: Conference attendance was reported at about four thousand by one outlet (internationalviewpoint.org result title); not independently counted. Editorial line is pro-union and left-leaning.

name: AFL-CIO
what: The US federation of 60-plus unions; runs organizing campaigns, a union-finder and join pages, and community programs including Working America.
scope: national (with state federations and local central labor councils)
legal_status: Labor federation, generally treated as a 501(c)(5); EIN not read
partisanship: Labor federation; endorses candidates (mostly Democratic); not nonpartisan
tax_deductible: Dues and contributions to labor organizations are generally not charitable deductions (not verified for this entry)
cost: Free to use site; membership comes through an affiliated union
status_2026: Press release on 2025 union organizing results (Common Dreams copy dated Feb 18, 2026); 2026 convention EC report PDF uploaded July 2026; Minnesota Reformer June 7, 2026 on a 2-million-worker organizing goal; People's World item on 22,500 election workers by July 3.
notes: Working America (AFL-CIO community affiliate for non-union members) was checked separately and dropped for lack of a dated 2026 item. Also an electoral actor through its political arm.

name: UE (United Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers of America)
what: Independent, member-run union with an organizing program and steward/organizer workshops; takes workers from any industry.
legal_status: Labor union, generally treated as a 501(c)(5); EIN not read
partisanship: Describes itself as rank-and-file and independent of political parties (check site for exact wording)
cost: Dues if workers win a contract; no charge to ask for organizing help (not verified)
status_2026: UE News 2026 item: Locals 228 and 728 joint steward/organizer workshop; Eastern Region newsletter Spring 2026 (PDF uploaded March 2026).
notes: Small relative to SEIU/Teamsters. SEIU, Teamsters and CWA join/organize pages were checked: CWA has a 2026 member publication but all three were cut for the 35-entry cap or lack of a dated 2026 item.

name: Workers Defense Project
what: Texas worker center that helps low-wage and construction workers recover unpaid wages, win safety protections and organize.
legal_status: 501(c)(3) per GuideStar profile for EIN 35-2296166 (profile URL only; page not read); affiliated Workers Defense Action Fund is the political arm (type not confirmed)
partisanship: Pro-worker; Action Fund makes electoral endorsements
tax_deductible: Donations to the (c)(3) are likely deductible; Action Fund is not (not verified)
status_2026: Workers Defense Action Fund endorsement reported Jan 29, 2026 (Style Magazine); Texas Observer tag page; NLRB case listing.
notes: Freedom Inc (Madison worker-center style group) was dropped; see dropped list.

name: NLRB: Steps to forming a union (federal guide)
what: Federal agency's plain-language guide, in many languages, to how workers petition for and hold a union election.
legal_status: US government agency (not a nonprofit)
partisanship: Nonpartisan government agency
status_2026: Agency site and multilingual 'Steps to forming a union' PDFs are indexed; a workcenter.gov page for the guide surfaced with a 'Lapse in Appropriations' title, so availability may be interrupted. No 2026-dated page for the guide itself was read.
notes: Check current NLRB quorum and case-processing status before relying on it: not verified here. Link the live NLRB page rather than a PDF.

name: Project Equity
what: Nonprofit that helps retiring business owners sell to their employees (employee ownership) and trains advisors.

legal_status: Believed 501(c)(3); EIN not read

cost: Free guides; fee-based advising for businesses
status_2026: Greater Washington employee-ownership ecosystem post; Rutgers EO Hub owner decision guide PDF dated 08.03.26 (third party); press-release page.
notes: Seed Commons (co-op conversion lender) was dropped: only a 2025 impact report surfaced.

name: Faith in Action (formerly PICO National Network)
what: Federation of local, congregation-based organizing groups that train leaders and run issue campaigns.

name: Gamaliel

name: Catholic Campaign for Human Development (US Conference of Catholic Bishops)
what: Bishops' anti-poverty program that funds community-organizing and economic-development groups led by low-income people.

name: Rural Organizing Project

status_2026: Annual Report 2025 PDF; Convergence article on 2026 midterm takeaways.

status_2026: Events calendar pages for workshops dated Jan, Mar and May 2026; a 2026 convention report podcast episode.
